findings.F1: The failing measures (Calmar 0.31, Sharpe below holding's) come from cases where the bounce has already recovered the coin's past week. Cases whose 5-day return, including the up day, is still negative are followed by a next-day short excess of +2.79 % (t 4.82, n 120, hit 71 %). Cases whose 5-day return is at or above 0 give +0.12 % (t 0.41, n 253). That is well under the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: Keeping only those still-down cases, with fees approximated, lifts the book's Sharpe from 0.59 to 1.37. Its deepest fall shrinks from -9.5 % to -2.4 %. Its Calmar rises from 0.40 to 2.27. This changes both failing measures.
findings.F3: The condition is not an effect of its own. On falling-market days with a negative 5-day return but no signal, the next-day short excess is +0.32 % (t 2.36, n 1504). The same days with the signal give +2.90 % (t 5.18, n 75). Signal days with a 5-day return at or above 0 give +0.28 % (t 0.65, n 156). The condition fits the brief's theory: a relief bounce that has not yet undone the recent fall is short-covering that gets given back, not a turn.
findings.F4: The effect grows with how far the coin is still down over 5 days. By quintile of the 5-day return, the short excess is +3.36 % (t 3.78), then +1.34 % (t 2.79), then -0.04 %, then -0.57 % from the lowest to the fourth quintile; the highest quintile gives +1.15 % (t 1.78).
findings.F5: The book's falls come from rebounds that kept going. Its 10 worst days fell on days when the coins rose +1 % to +15 %. The deepest fall (40 days, -9.4 %) sits in w13, where cases earned only +0.32 % (t 0.33, n 51) and only 35 % had a negative 5-day return. Among the 15 worst cases, only 33 % had a negative 5-day return; their mean 5-day return was +6.1 %.

findings.F7: In an agitated market (30-day swing above the 90-day swing, a proxy for the profile's agitation), cases give +2.04 % (t 3.40, n 72) against +0.73 % (t 2.30, n 301) when calm. The same agitated falling days without the signal give -0.20 % (t -1.00, n 841), so agitation is not the effect by itself.
findings.F8: The idea's own grading by width does not hold. By width quartile, the excess is +1.32 %, +1.23 %, +0.23 % and +1.60 %. Among the still-down cases, the narrowest tercile earns the most (+4.32 %, t 3.94).

ideas.idea: In a falling market, an up day whose high-to-low range is wide against the coin's average daily range over the past 20 days and that closes near its high, while the coin's 5-day return including that day is still negative, is followed by a fall over the next day. The more the coin is still down over those 5 days, the larger the next day's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should sell for one day only into wide downtrend rallies that have not yet recovered the past week's losses, and stand aside when the bounce has already lifted the coin above where it was 5 days ago.
ideas.name: still-down wide bounce fade

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, an up day whose high-to-low range is wide against the coin's average daily range over the past 20 days and that closes near its high is followed by a fall over the next day. The wider that day's range and the nearer its close to the high, the larger the next day's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should keep the one-day fade of wide high-closing rallies for downtrends that are swinging more than usual, where forced covering overshoots most.
ideas.name: agitated downtrend bounce fade
